title: The Taoist Priest of Mount Lao
lines: A young man named Wang Qi went to Mount Lao seeking to learn magic from a famous immortal. For months, the immortal made him chop wood and fetch water. Wang Qi grew impatient.
'Master, teach me something — anything! I did not come here to be a woodcutter.' The immortal smiled and taught him a single spell: how to walk through walls.

Wang Qi returned home bursting with pride. 'Wife! Wife! Watch this!' He backed up, chanted the spell, and ran headfirst at the wall. He struck it with a sickening crack and fell to the ground, a giant swelling rising on his forehead.
His wife helped him up, laughing. 'Fool,' she said. 'You learned nothing because you were too impatient to learn anything.' Wang Qi never spoke of his 'magic' again.
Moral: The impatient student gains only a bump on the head.
